revisionHistory.summary: The three panels became ONE. One route, one AuthenticationPanel with four states, one AuthenticationPage split into a drawing half and a connected half.
retained: every tree 1.1 approved: the shortcut over the divider, the credential form, the code step with its cooldown and its way back, the confirmation, and the question-and-answer footer
the reference's own rule that a different tree is a state and the same tree with a different sentence is props
the uncontrolled ref, the browser-side password comparison, and the single refusal sentence covering both ways the reset's second step can fail
Google as the only provider, from 1.1
rejected: three routes - starci has exactly one authentication address, and the mode is panel state rather than a URL. Keeping three was what made this case not the reference it named.

OtpStep as a separate owner - it existed only because two panels each needed a code step and a sixty-second cooldown; with one panel there is exactly one of each, and a block extracted to be shared once is a block that should not have been extracted

a mode STATE - which journey is running changes which fields appear inside the same tree, which is props by the reference's own rule; making it a state would have given the union twelve members drawing four trees
revisionHistory.reason: The named reference is one route whose panel switches mode in place. Revisions 1.0 and 1.1 shipped three panels across three routes and read as a family that merely resembled it. 1.2 is the consolidation verdict applied: MERGE, on the fact that `details`, `code` and `done` are the same three trees in all three journeys.
consequences: SignInPanel, SignUpPanel, ForgotPasswordPanel and OtpStep are all gone; `apps/app/src/components/blocks/auth/SignInPanel/component.tsx` was deleted in the Apply commit

REMEMBER-ME IS BACK. 1.1 recorded its absence as a divergence from the parity baseline; the merged panel restores it on the sign-in mode only, and the refresh cookie still has a fixed thirty-day lifetime, so the control records intent and changes nothing server-side yet

THE PROVIDER SHORTCUT NOW APPEARS ON THE RESET JOURNEY. In one panel the shortcut block sits above the divider inside the single `details` tree, so it is drawn for every mode - which is what the reference does and the exact reverse of open question 3's answer in 1.0
the divider label is set in capitals (`HOẶC` / `OR`), matching the parity baseline
AuthenticationPage is split: `component.tsx` draws from a finished panel prop and `index.tsx` resolves the world - seven mutations, one challenge, one cooldown clock and the mode
`isCredentialsOpen` and the sign-in-closed state are gone: with one surface there is nothing to collapse, and the credential form is always mounted and always open
the scoped CSS stand-in for the card inset is gone from the candidate's `globals.css`, because the inset was really applied to `authentication-panel-card` in the registry

parityBaseline.head: 8410a74

divergences.what: signing in does not pass through a mailed code
divergences.why: THE ONE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE LEFT, and it is the backend's rather than a choice. nivo's `signIn` exchanges a password for a session in one request; the reference's backend mails a code for every journey. So signIn runs details -> done, and only signUp and forgotPassword reach the code step.

divergences.what: an account owing TOTP lands on a twoFactorUnsupported notice instead of a second-factor step
divergences.why: `signIn` answers `requiresTwoFactor` and nothing in this build can complete the challenge. Reusing the refusal sentence would tell those readers their password was wrong, which it was not.
neither repository has a terms or privacy route - the reference's own links resolve to nothing

divergences.what: the resend control states a cooldown
divergences.why: nivo's backend enforces OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS = 60s and the reference's backend does not

divergences.what: the confirmation on the reset journey sends the reader to sign in
divergences.why: forgotPasswordVerifyOtp answers a boolean, not a session
requested in revision 1.1; GitHub is gone from the panel, the catalogue and the registry's restingCount

divergences.what: remember-me is drawn but changes nothing server-side
divergences.why: restored in 1.2 to match the reference's row, while the refresh cookie's maxAge is a fixed thirty days with no per-request control. Recorded as a backend enabler rather than removed, because the control has to exist before the cookie change has anywhere to land.

evidence.claim: byte-identical, 26292 bytes. Apply ported the candidate's tree rather than reinterpreting a screenshot, and the difference between the two files is zero rather than small.
25 passing assertions, including every refusal this candidate draws: wrong code, replay, cooldown, unknown challenge, weak password.
an unknown address answers identically to a known one - same flag, sentence, TTL and mailed code - and the refusal arrives only after the code is proved.
ONE panel on ONE route, whose mode switches in place; the code step is one Field with kind:"code"; there is no step indicator and no digit row. This is the fact revision 1.2 acted on.
the visible card is SurfaceFormCard at the page, not classes on the contract entry.
kind:"code" maps to type=text, autocomplete=one-time-code, inputmode=numeric.
nivo zeroes the vendor card's padding on purpose and hands the interior to the entry, which is why the entry declares the p-4 inset itself.
57 starci-fe rules present and all 57 at error, with noInlineConfig true; 19 candidate ts/tsx files are matched by the lint glob, so the clean run is real rather than an unmatched glob.
`requiresTwoFactor` is read BEFORE `accessToken`, so a two-factor challenge cannot be mistaken for a session.

unknowns: Whether `requestPasswordReset` and `resetPassword` stay in the transport after this, since nothing calls them any more.
Whether sign-up should collect a display name - signUpInit accepts an optional `name` and the reference does not ask for one.

Whether the provider shortcut BELONGS on the reset journey. The merge put it there structurally rather than by decision, and 1.0's objection still stands on its own terms: a provider button does not recover this account, it signs the reader into a different one. Suppressing it again would mean a mode-conditional shortcut block, which is a product choice nobody has made.

Whether five of the fourteen sealed screenshots are re-rendered. See screenshotProvenance: they were exported before the last two copy edits of revision 1.2 and therefore show a lowercase divider label and, on the two sign-in states, no remember-me row.

decisions.decision: ONE panel rather than three, and the step is the state while the mode is not
decisions.tradeoff: one union of four members instead of three unions of two, and every state now has to say which mode it is in. In exchange the sixty-second cooldown, the uncontrolled ref, the mismatch check and the status slot exist exactly once.

decisions.decision: OtpStep is retired rather than kept as a shared child
decisions.tradeoff: the code step's tree now lives inside the same file as the details tree. It was extracted in 1.0 so two panels could share it; with one panel a shared child would be a block rendered by exactly one caller, which canon reads as a seam invented for its own sake.

decisions.decision: the page is split into component.tsx and index.tsx
decisions.tradeoff: two files where 1.1 had one. The drawing half needs no locale, no session and no request to draw any state, which is what lets the state matrix be rendered without standing the world up first; the connected half owns the seven mutations, the challenge handle and the cooldown clock.

decisions.decision: the panel prop is passed WHOLE rather than unpacked into a dozen props
decisions.tradeoff: component.tsx takes a type it cannot inspect. The panel's own union is what guarantees the copy of a state it is not drawing cannot be supplied; splitting it here would hand this file the job of reassembling it, and every reassembly is a chance to get it wrong.

decisions.decision: one refusal sentence covers both ways the reset's second step can fail
decisions.tradeoff: a legitimate reader with a typo is told less than the backend knows, which is the price of not letting an inbox holder enumerate accounts. `result.reason` is deliberately discarded at that one call site.

decisions.decision: the password confirmation is checked in the browser and never sent
decisions.tradeoff: none - no request answers it, and sending a mismatched pair would spend a code to learn what a comparison already knew

decisions.decision: the cooldown is counted in the page, not asked for
decisions.tradeoff: a LOCAL clock that may drift from the server's. The refusal `OTP_RESEND_TOO_SOON_EXCEPTION` is still handled, because a countdown that disagrees is not a reason to stop reading the answer.
a reader who switches away mid-challenge spends a code for nothing. A challenge belongs to one address on one journey, and carrying it across would offer a code that cannot finish where they now are.

decisions.decision: the transport GAINS six OTP operations; nothing existing in it changes
decisions.tradeoff: the plan record said "transport untouched", which was true of the sign-in path and not of the file. Corrected in 1.0 rather than left to Apply.

build.note: Re-run against the merged panel. The previous log recorded a FAILURE: a concurrent change gave `centred-title-pair` an optional `mark` slot, and omitting the key made every defineContractComponent in the panel fail to resolve its overload. one route per STATE rather than one route for the screen. The target is a single `/authentication`; each candidate URL exists only so a static export can seal one state, and every one of them mounts the same page with different props.

The OAuth round trip has no client id, no PKCE verifier and no callback route in this build, so the screen REPORTS rather than pretends - a screen that looked connected and was not is the kind of thing that gets believed.

GONE. The link-based reset left the union in 1.1 when the journey became code-based, and 1.2 has no link journey at all - `requestPasswordReset` and `resetPassword` survive in the transport with no caller.

consolidation.distinguishingFact: THE FACT THAT MADE THEM ONE: `details`, `code` and `done` are the SAME THREE TREES in all three journeys. What differs between the journeys is which fields appear inside those trees and which words label them - and by the reference's own rule, which this case adopted in 1.0, a different tree is a state while the same tree with a different sentence is props. Three panels were therefore three copies of one state machine, each re-deriving the same union, the same uncontrolled ref and the same status slot. Merging also retires OtpStep on its own terms: it was extracted in 1.0 because two panels each needed the code step and its sixty-second cooldown, and with one panel there is exactly one of each - a block shared by a single caller is a seam kept for its own sake.
consolidation.whatMergingCostChecked: The 1.0 verdicts that said keep-apart were re-read rather than overruled by convenience. SignUpPanel was kept apart on a DIFFERENT DOMAIN ENTITY (an account, not a session) and a third field existing only to be compared with the second; ForgotPasswordPanel on a constraint neither sibling has (it must never disclose whether an address is registered). Both facts are still true and both are now expressed as props inside one panel: `mode` selects the third field, and the reset journey's conditional subtitle and single refusal sentence carry the non-disclosure rule. A fact that can be expressed as a prop of one owner was never a reason for a second owner - it was a reason for a discriminator, which is what `mode` is.

consolidation.distinguishingFact: Three pages differed only in which panel they mounted and which mutations they called. With one panel there is one thing to mount, and the three mutation sets are three branches of one submit - so the pages collapsed the same way the panels did. The named reference has exactly one authentication address, and a page per journey was the thing that made three URLs necessary in the first place.
Retired into AuthenticationPanel's `code` state. It was a correct extraction while two panels shared it and became a block with one caller the moment they became one panel.
